title: 6.28.2 Sub-build: Pick up and put down
description: One token on a small board: a click becomes a row and a column, a click on the token picks it up, and a click one square diagonally away puts it down there.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: A red token sits in the bottom-left corner. Clicking does nothing yet: the `if (mouse.presses())` block is empty.

steps.title: Where was the click?
steps.instructions: Inside `if (mouse.presses())`, turn the click into a square: `const c = floor(mouse.x / CELL);` and `const r = floor(mouse.y / CELL);`. Then pick the token up when the click is on it: `if (r === pr && c === pc) picked = true;`. Run and click the token: its square lights up gold.
hints: This board starts at the top of the canvas, so there is no `TOP` to take off.
`pr` and `pc` are the token's row and column (p for piece). They are not the reading's `tr` and `tc`: those mean the square a move goes to.

steps.title: Put it down
steps.instructions: Add an `else if` to that test: `else if (picked && abs(r - pr) === 1 && abs(c - pc) === 1) { pr = r; pc = c; picked = false; }`. Run: pick the token up and click a square one step diagonally away. It moves there and the light goes out. A click two squares away, or straight up, does nothing.
hints: `abs` drops the minus sign, so one test covers all four diagonal neighbours.
This token may go backward too. In the lab, `moveKind` adds the rule that a piece only goes forward.

requirements.title: A click becomes a row and a column
requirements.description: The click position is divided by the square size and cut down with floor. Help: 6.28.1 (Reading: From a click to a square, and one rule function)

requirements.title: A click on the token picks it up
requirements.description: Clicking the token marks it as picked up. Help: 6.28.1 (Reading: From a click to a square, and one rule function)
requirements.hint: if (r === pr && c === pc) picked = true;

requirements.title: One square diagonally
requirements.description: The token moves only to a square one row and one column away, tested with abs or another way. Help: 6.28.1 (Reading: From a click to a square, and one rule function)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: Pick up and put down". The task: on a click, turn mouse.x and mouse.y into a row and a column with floor, pick the token up when the click is on it, and when it is picked up move it to a clicked square one row and one column away (abs, or another correct test). Accept any names, helpers, ternaries, nested ifs, switch statements and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.
